title: Local demographic reorganization does not scale into a transferable island-resilience rule in Antarctic penguins
core_claim_unchanged: Palmer within-island concentration is strongly supported; static Antarctic-wide island architecture does not yield a confirmed transferable response rule.
new_secondary_result: Palmer performance-linked lag-2/3 redistribution is locally informative under a fixed specification, but the prospectively frozen Signy lag-2 primary replication is unsupported.

palmer_lag2.provenance: fixed-specification validation after exposed provenance repair

manuscript_role: one secondary Results subsection plus one Discussion paragraph; detailed mechanism diagnostics remain Supplementary.
claim_boundaries: Do not call Palmer a win-stay/lose-switch mechanism.
Do not call Signy an independent positive replication.
Do not promote the comment-filter Signy sensitivity over the frozen primary.
Do not infer individual breeding dispersal, prospecting, cue use, mortality or temporary nonbreeding from colony counts.
Do not let this secondary dynamic analysis rescue the non-confirmatory Antarctic-wide static-trait hypothesis.
